The next successor writes a V4-B3 authorization task-pack before any code.

The five B3 product decisions are already settled and the task-pack records them: one authenticated read-only Workbench HTTP route; canonical default workspace only; mandatory verifyExportedBundle before any response; NO redaction in B3; and mandatory count plus serialized-byte ceilings that fail closed rather than returning a partial bundle.

B3 exports an internal, full trust artifact. Public-safe and redacted receipt formats are V5-PR3 work (issue #276). Canonical receipt content including metadata participates in hash semantics, so stripping fields during a B3 export would break chain validation or amount to defining a new public receipt format.
The task-pack must justify its own ceiling numbers; the roadmap mandates that ceilings exist, not what they are.
exportMaterializedReceiptBundle and verifyExportedBundle already exist and are proved by tests; V4-B3 is a reachability gap, not a missing primitive.

The user-reachable receipt surface today is read-only: GET /api/trust-receipt, GET /api/trust-receipt/:receiptId and GET /api/workbench/trust-receipt/:receiptId, plus a receipt-exporter plugin that writes single receipts to files rather than a chain-validated bundle.
